Q13
Consider the following statements :
(i) Auto increment addressing mode is useful in
creating self-relocating code.
(ii) If auto increment addressing mode is included
in an instruction set architecture, then an
additional ALU is required for effective address
calculation.
(iii) In auto increment addressing mode, the
amount of increment depends on the size of the
data item accessed.
Which of the above statements is/are true?
Choose the correct answer from the code given
below :

explanation.value:
Option C is Correct
Statement (i): Auto increment addressing mode is
useful in creating self-relocating code.
Auto increment addressing mode automatically
updates the address pointer after accessing a
memory location. This is useful in iterating
through arrays or data structures, but it does not
directly facilitate self-relocating code.
Self-relocating code refers to code that can
adjust itself to execute properly regardless of
where it is loaded in memory. Auto increment
addressing does not inherently assist in achieving
this.
Hence, This statement is false.
Statement (ii): If auto increment addressing mode
is included in an instruction set architecture, then
an additional ALU is required for effective
address calculation.
In auto increment addressing mode, the effective
address is calculated by adding a fixed or
variable increment to the current value of the
address pointer. This operation requires an
arithmetic addition.
An additional ALU may not always be required;
this depends on the hardware design. Many
processors reuse the existing ALU for both
effective address computation and general
arithmetic operations.
However, in some architectures, a separate unit
may be provided for this purpose.
Hence, This statement is not universally true and
is false for most modern architectures.
Statement (iii): In auto increment addressing
mode, the amount of increment depends on the
size of the data item accessed.
In most architectures, the auto increment amount
depends on the size of the data being accessed
(e.g., a 4-byte increment for a 32-bit integer or a
1-byte increment for a character).
This ensures that the next memory address
points to the subsequent data item.
Hence, This statement is true.
